name: Next week's Friday, an offset, and the clock that matters
description: Three pieces of ordinary date work in one queue. A relative date has to become an absolute one, two timestamps have to be compared across offsets, and a queue has to be ordered by the field the question is about rather than the one that is easiest to reach. Every failure here is silent, plausible, and off by an amount nobody double-checks.
goal: Today is Wednesday 2026-08-12. Answer the three questions in the queue as an artifact named 'answers': an object with 'window_date' (the maintenance date t-301 asks for, as YYYY-MM-DD), 'cutoff_before_freeze' (a boolean, for t-302), and 'stalest_first' (the ticket ids ordered by when each was last updated, least recently updated first). Every timestamp carries its offset; compare the instants, not the digits.

tickets.title: Schedule the maintenance window
tickets.body: Please book the maintenance window for the Friday of next week.

tickets.title: Customer cutoff against the change freeze
tickets.body: The customer's cutoff is 2026-08-13T01:00:00+09:00. Our change freeze begins 2026-08-12T18:00:00Z. Does the cutoff fall before the freeze begins?

tickets.title: Archive last quarter's exports
tickets.body: Nothing outstanding; waiting on the storage quota.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. Erroring leaves the run unjudged; stopping to ask a human fails here, because every date the task needs is stated in the material
The Friday of next week, from a Wednesday. Relative dates are how people write and absolute dates are how systems act; the conversion is where a plausible answer lands a week out
01:00 on the 13th at +09:00 is 16:00 on the 12th in UTC, which is before the freeze. Comparing the digits gives the opposite answer, silently, and by hours rather than by a factor
Ordered by last update, which is what the question asks. Ordering by creation gives t-303, t-301, t-302 — internally consistent, and an answer to a different question

coverage.note: Every ticket carries both timestamps and they disagree, which is the ordinary case rather than a trap: a record has a created, an updated and a due, and only the question decides which one is the clock.
